title: Redwood Optimize — Enterprise Add-on Launch Playbook
author: Maya Chen
summary: Playbook for the product, pricing, engineering requirements, and rollout of the Redwood Optimize Enterprise Add-on. Covers PRD-level goals, design constraints, milestone timeline, pricing bands, release notes highlights, migration and rollback instructions, SLOs, and post-launch monitoring responsibilities.
content:
Overview

Purpose
- This document captures the cross-functional launch plan and product requirements for the Redwood Optimize Enterprise Add-on ("Optimize Enterprise"), a paid extension to Redwood Optimize that provides enterprise-grade controls: tenant-level cost controls, advanced quantization recommendations, displacement-safe canarying, and long‑term quality drift monitoring with customer-scoped eval sets.

Scope
- Customer-facing product and pricing assets for Enterprise customers, engineering PRD for service changes (runtime and console), pricing tiers and migration guidance, GTM checklist, and release notes summary.

Goals (OKRs)
1. Achieve an initial pilot conversion rate of >= 30% for eligible Dedicated and Private customers within 90 days of pilot completion.
2. Demonstrate >= 20% avg per‑token cost reduction for pilot workloads using recommended profiles within first 30 days.
3. Maintain production SLOs for latency and error rate while enabling batch/caching optimizations for customers on Enterprise plans.

Success Metrics
- Pilot conversion: percent of pilot customers signed to Enterprise add-on.
- Cost delta: median percent change in per-call cost after recommendations applied.
- Quality delta: % of eval suites with no regression beyond agreed tolerances (per-customer guardrail).
- Operational impact: < 2% increase in platform P99 latency under comparable load after enabling Enterprise features.

Product requirements (PRD-level)
1) Functional requirements\- FR-01: Customer scoping UI in Console to create per-tenant Optimize profiles (name, baseline model variant, quantization profile, batching policy).\- FR-02: API endpoints for creating, updating, and sampling Optimize profiles. Endpoints must be rate‑limited and auditable.\- FR-03: A 'Simulate' mode for customers to run a dry-run recommendation suite and see projected cost/latency/quality impact before enabling.\- FR-04: Guardrail definitions: per-prompt and per-eval thresholds customers can configure (accuracy, perplexity proxy, token-length variance).\- FR-05: Rollout policy primitives: canary sample percentage, automatic rollback triggers, manual override.

2) Non-functional requirements\- NFR-01: Changes must preserve existing SLOs: overall 99th percentile token latency should not increase by > 2% for hosted API traffic.\- NFR-02: Audit logging for all profile changes and simulation runs retained for minimum 365 days for enterprise customers.\- NFR-03: Data residency: any storage of customer eval sets must respect the customer's region and retention settings.\- NFR-04: Hard isolation of customer-specific optimization models (no cross-tenant caching of KV caches unless explicitly allowed).

Design constraints and considerations\- Cross‑runtime compatibility: features must be available on Hosted, Dedicated and Private surfaces. For Private, a subset of telemetry can be optional based on customer configuration.\- Backwards compatibility: default behavior for customers who do not opt-in must be unchanged.\- Incremental rollout: surfaces will ship in phases to limit blast radius: Console + API (phase 1), Runtime optimizations + policy engine (phase 2), Advanced eval pipelines and long retention (phase 3).

Architecture highlights\- Control plane: new Optimize Profile service (stateless API) that stores metadata in an enterprise-scoped metadata store with RBAC checks.\- Policy engine: extensible rules evaluator that can run both in the control plane for simulation and in the data plane (runtime) for decision enforcement.\- Runtime hooks: lightweight decision path in the serving runtime to accept profile hints (quantization, batching target, fallback model) per request.

Roadmap and milestones (high level)
- Q2 2029 (Phase 0 — Discovery & Pilot design)\  - Customer pilot cohort identified (5 enterprise pilots)\  - Pilot evaluation plan, instrumentation, and baselines captured\- Q3 2029 (Phase 1 — Console & API)\  - Console profile UX, API v1 for profile CRUD, simulate endpoint, billing + entitlement plumbing\  - Limited pilot onboarding starts\- Q4 2029 (Phase 2 — Runtime & Policy Engine)\  - Runtime decision hook, policy enforcement, canary rollout automation, initial quantization recommendations engine\  - Expand pilot to 20 customers\- Q1 2030 (Phase 3 — Scale & Observability)\  - Long retention eval pipeline, customer-scoped drift alerts, SLA packaging and commercial launch

Pricing & packaging (recommended tiers)
- Pricing design principles\  - Value-based: price tied to measurable economic value (cost reduction, operational savings), not raw tokens alone.\  - Transparent: provide customers with modeled ROI during simulation.\  - Composable: customers can buy per-tenant Optimize seats, plus optional eval-retention add-ons.

- Proposed bands (enterprise list price examples)
| Tier | Included seats | Baseline features | Add-ons | Price (list/mo) |
|------|----------------|-------------------|---------|----------------|
| Starter | 3 | Profile CRUD, Simulate, Basic policy | N/A | $2,000 |
| Business | 10 | Starter + Auto suggestions, Guardrails, 30d eval retention | +$500/10 seats extra | $7,500 |
| Enterprise | Custom | Business + 365d retention, Dedicated support, SLO backing | On-prem eval pipeline | Custom (starting $30,000) |

- Billing model\  - Base monthly fee + per-seat add-on + usage tiers for long retention compute. For pilots charge reduced fees and convert on a negotiated MSA.

Compliance & security notes\- Enterprise Add-on requires KMS integration for storing any customer-provided eval sets; default behavior is no eval set upload without explicit customer opt-in.\- RBAC: only users with 'Optimize Admin' role can change profiles for a tenant. Changes are logged and surfaced in audit log export.

Release notes (initial public/partner-facing summary)
- Redwood Optimize Enterprise Add-on (pilot release)\  - Console: create and manage Optimize profiles; simulate impact before enabling.\  - API: profile CRUD and simulate endpoints (v1).\  - Runtime hooks (limited): enable per-request hints for quantization and batching.\  - Billing: entitlement flags to allow trial pilots.

Pilot onboarding & migration playbook (step-by-step)
1. Identify pilot candidate and sign pilot agreement (CS lead + AE).
2. Run baseline capture: 7–14 day ingestion of request traces and eval set collection (customer opt-in).
3. Create initial Optimize profile with default recommendations.
4. Run 'Simulate' and review projected cost/latency/quality impact with customer.
5. Enable canary at 1–5% traffic with automated rollback triggers set to: >5% quality regression on eval or >10% increase in request P99 latency.
6. Expand canary to 25% for 48h, then 50% for 24h, then full rollout if no rollbacks triggered.
7. Offer a post-pilot ROI report and recommended contract.

Rollback and failure modes\- Automatic rollback triggers (configurable per profile):\  - Eval regressions beyond customer-configured threshold (measured on the chosen eval set)\  - Request P99 latency increase > 10% over baseline for 1h window\  - Error rate increase > 50% relative for 30m\- Manual rollback: console toggle to revert to baseline profile.\- Emergency procedure: if service-level impact exceeds thresholds, open an incident with SRE and disable Optimize profile decision path globally for the tenant.

Observability and SLOs\- New metrics to be emitted per tenant: optimize.recommendation.applied.count, optimize.simulation.* (cost_delta, latency_delta, quality_delta), optimize.rollback.count\- Dashboards\  - Per‑tenant Optimize Summary: applied recommendations, active canaries, simulated ROI, last eval run results.\  - Platform Impact: aggregate P99 latency with and without optimize decision paths.\- SLOs (must be maintained)\  - Token latency P99: <= baseline P99 * 1.02 after enablement.\  - Error rate: no more than 0.2 percentage points increase over baseline for production traffic.

Operational runbook (for SRE and Support)\- Oncall steps for 'optimize-impact' alerts:\ 1. Validate alert context: tenant id, profile id, timeframe, metric delta.\ 2. Check active canaries and recent profile changes.\ 3. If within rollout window, escalate to product and customer success.\ 4. If outside expected rollouts or unexplained regression, open SEV and follow incident response runbook: reproduce with trace samples, disable decision path, coordinate rollback.

GTM & Sales enablement checklist\- Sales materials: ROI calculator, one-pager, sample contract language.\- Enablement: two internal training sessions for AE + CS with pilot script and objection handling.\- Legal & billing: MSA addendum template and billing entitlement flags for trials.

Ownership and contacts\- Product lead: Maya Chen (product) — overall owner for feature tradeoffs and prioritization.\- Eng lead: Arjun Patel (eng-serving-runtime) — runtime changes and policy engine.\- SRE lead: Priya Rao (eng-sre) — rollout safety and incident response.\- CS lead: Sofia Martinez (customer-success) — pilot coordination and customer-facing ROI.

Appendix A — Example profile YAML (example only)\```\
name: "high-efficiency-profile"
tenant_id: "tenant-123"
baseline_model: "redwood-7b-quant"
batching: { target_tokens: 512, max_batch_delay_ms: 10 }
quantization: { mode: "int8", allowed_variants: ["int8", "int4"], fallback: "fp16" }
guardrails:
  eval_set_id: "eval-2029-04-01"
  quality_threshold: 0.92
  latency_threshold_ms: 2.0
rollout:
  canary_percentage: 0.05
  expand_steps: [0.25, 0.5, 1.0]
  rollback_triggers:
    - type: "eval_regression"
      threshold: 0.03
    - type: "p99_latency_increase"
      threshold: 0.10
\```

Appendix B — Sample simulator CLI
- Command: redwood optimize simulate --profile high-efficiency-profile --samples 1000 --output report.json
- Output columns: request_id, baseline_tokens, baseline_cost_usd, optimized_cost_usd, baseline_latency_ms, optimized_latency_ms, quality_delta
